method: Reduce integer event/error bookkeeping on CUDA and reuse scratch allocations between molecular chunks.

workload.recording_source: 320x180 RGB quadrant exposure at 20 fps: 100 ms dark, left-white, right-white, gray128, dark.
workload.description: Same previously saved eight named receptors and seeds; 30,000 microvilli each.

focused_tests.scope: Existing ordinary GPU batch independence/continuation and single-receptor chunking/reset/darkness checks; no new stress or extreme-case tests.

checks: native preparation runs separately with progress while body and brain stay at time zero
prepared IDs, intensities, photons, channels and voltage match the previous offline recording exactly
native loader selects prepared sources at time zero with a video preview and real OpenGL brain
pause and release freeze brain, body, receptor clock and frame without resetting neural voltage
recording endpoint pauses exactly, with zero source/relay spikes and synchronized body and brain clocks
native full-brain final voltages and counts match the offline replay exactly
Reset clears the recording, source clamps and graded mode and restores normal video controls

limits: Two warm paired timings on one physical RTX 4060 Laptop GPU, with reversed order. The small measured difference is sensitive to power and scheduling.
Timings include ten 50 ms advance calls, exclude construction, stream initialization, compilation, GUI and archive export.
Bookkeeping bytes exclude photon input, channel traces and molecular-state transfers. This is not a 30,000-fold runtime speedup.
Same uncalibrated exposure and existing molecular, membrane and release models; no physiological accuracy or live-vision claim.
Native source-app check on Linux; no new packaged build or macOS GPU check.

The initial native check terminated with exit 143 after stalling without a completed response. A rerun with temporary progress logging passed without model changes; the initial stall cause was not established.
